newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks post record despite profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks post record despite profit taking.

text.p: After a brief consolidation the day before, Swiss shares regained power on Wednesday and posted another record close despite late profit taking that triggered a slide from the day's high.
Dealers said the market was nervous and trade was heavily influenced by hedging transactions, which put SMI futures and several stocks such as Nestle and UBS under pressure.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) added 34.8 points or 0.77 percent to 4,525.5.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 16.97 points or 0.59 percent to 2,870.95.
February SMI futures were up 38 points to 4,526.
"The rally could last for a long time," one trader said, addding that investors did not really have any alternatives to shares.
"Although peope are getting dizzy on such levels, they get used to it after a while," he said.

Novartis was actively traded, still profiting from Tuesday's details about the imminent spin off of subsidiary Ciba Speciality Chemicals. Novartis registereds soared 20 francs, or 1.14 percent, to 1,777.
Clariant also gained more ground on Ciba Specialty Chemicals news, adding 22 francs to 716. Roche certificates were up 215 francs to 12,785.
UBS ended up two francs to 1,297 ahead of the release of the bank's 1996 figures on Friday.

Traders said there were hopes in the market that UBS's extraordinary loss for 1996 could be smaller than expected. The bank last November said it expected a loss of about half a billion Swiss francs due to one-off restructuring charges of three billion francs.
CS Group also firmed while SBC traded flat.
Chemical firm EMS was amonG the day's favourites, advancing 120 francs to 5,770.
Nestle fell one franc to 1,640. ABB gave up seven francs to 1,822.
